info.title: Jx Finance API
info.description: Personal and household finance ledger. Every route lives under /api and answers JSON. Money is carried as a decimal string with at most two decimal places so nothing is lost to floating point; dates are YYYY-MM-DD in the instance time zone. Collections that can grow are paged with page and pageSize and answer with items, page, pageSize, and total. Authentication is a session cookie from POST /api/auth/login, so browser clients must send credentials. Failures answer application/problem+json with a machine-readable code per error; see the ProblemDetails schema.

post.description: Opens a new account. A personal account belongs to you alone; a shared account must name a household you are a member of, and everyone in that household sees it and its transactions. The starting balance is the balance before any transaction is recorded.

201.description: The account was created. The Location header points at it.

400.description: Validation failed, or the named household is not one of yours.

get.description: Returns the accounts you can see: your own plus the shared accounts of your households, each with its current balance. Filters are optional and combine with AND.

parameters.name: search
parameters.description: Case-insensitive match against the account name.

parameters.name: iban
parameters.description: Case-insensitive match against the IBAN.

parameters.name: type
parameters.description: Keep only accounts of this type.

parameters.name: sort
parameters.description: Field to sort by. Defaults to creation order.

parameters.name: direction
parameters.description: Asc or Desc. Defaults to Asc.

delete.description: Archives the account instead of deleting it: the transactions posted to it stay in the ledger and in reports, but the account no longer appears in listings or pickers.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: The account id.

404.description: No such account is visible to the signed-in user.

get.description: Returns a single account with its current balance. An account that belongs to another user, or to a household you are not a member of, is reported as missing rather than forbidden, so the endpoint cannot be used to probe for other people's data.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: The account id.

404.description: No such account is visible to the signed-in user.

put.description: Replaces the editable fields of an account. Moving an account from Personal to Shared hands its history to the household; moving it back makes it private again. Transactions already posted to the account keep their amounts.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: The account id. Takes precedence over the id in the body.

400.description: Validation failed, or the named household is not one of yours.

404.description: No such account is visible to the signed-in user.

post.description: Starts tracking something of value that is not an account balance. Its value counts towards net worth from the as-of date onwards.

201.description: The asset was created. The Location header points at it.

get.description: Returns the assets you track outside the ledger, such as property or vehicles, each with its latest valuation and the date that valuation is as of.

200.description: The assets belonging to the signed-in user.

delete.description: Stops tracking the asset. Snapshots already recorded keep the value it had.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: The asset id.

404.description: No such asset belongs to the signed-in user.

put.description: Revalues or renames an asset. Net worth uses the new value from the next read onwards; snapshots already taken keep the value that was current when they were written.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: The asset id. Takes precedence over the id in the body.

404.description: No such asset belongs to the signed-in user.

post.description: Removes the authenticator secret and the remaining recovery codes after re-authenticating with the account password. Rate limited to five attempts per five minutes.

404.description: The session points at a user that no longer exists.

429.description: Too many attempts; wait and retry.

post.description: Verifies the first code produced by the authenticator and turns two-factor authentication on. The response carries the one-time recovery codes; they are shown once and never again, so the client must make the user save them before moving on.

200.description: Two-factor authentication is on. The recovery codes are returned once.

400.description: The code did not match the pending secret.

404.description: The session points at a user that no longer exists.

post.description: Generates a fresh authenticator secret and returns it as both a shared key and an otpauth URI for a QR code. Nothing is enabled yet: enrolment only completes once the code from the authenticator is posted to the enable endpoint. Re-authentication with the account password is required, and the call is rate limited to five attempts per five minutes.

200.description: The shared key and otpauth URI to enrol with.

401.description: The password was wrong, or two-factor authentication is already enabled.

404.description: The session points at a user that no longer exists.

429.description: Too many attempts; wait and retry.

post.description: Exchanges an email and password for a short-lived access token and a refresh token, both set as HttpOnly cookies. When the account has two-factor authentication enabled and no code is supplied, the response is 200 with twoFactorRequired set and no cookie issued; repeat the call with twoFactorCode filled in. The code may be a six-digit authenticator code or an unused recovery code. Rate limited to 10 attempts per five minutes per client. Five wrong passwords or codes in a row lock the account for 15 minutes; until then every attempt answers 429 with code credentials.lockedOut.

200.description: Signed in, or a second factor is required. Check twoFactorRequired.

401.description: The credentials or the authenticator code were rejected.

429.description: Too many sign-in attempts from this client, or the account is locked after repeated failures; wait and retry.

post.description: Ends the session and clears its cookies. Safe to call when already signed out.

get.description: Returns the profile behind the current session cookie, including the role and whether two-factor authentication is on. The client uses this to decide what to render and to detect an expired session.

200.description: The profile of the signed-in user.

404.description: The session points at a user that no longer exists.

post.description: Exchanges the refresh cookie for a new access token cookie and a rotated refresh cookie. Call it when a request answers 401, then retry that request once. The session keeps its original absolute expiry; renewing never extends it. A session whose user was deactivated, locked out, or had their role or password changed elsewhere is rejected.

401.description: The refresh cookie is missing, expired, or revoked; sign in again.

429.description: Too many renewals; wait and retry.

post.summary: Take a backup of the whole installation
post.description: Administrators only. Writes every table of the installation into one gzip-compressed JSON file in the backup directory of the server: users with their password hashes, households, settings, exchange rates and all financial data of every user. Sign-in sessions are left out. The file is read from one database snapshot, so it is consistent even while others keep working. Broker tokens inside it stay encrypted with the key directory of this installation and have to be entered again on any other one.

403.description: Only administrators can take a backup.

429.description: More than 10 backups in five minutes; wait and retry.

get.summary: List the backups kept on the server
get.description: Administrators only. Returns every backup in the backup directory, newest first, with its size and row count. The first entry answers when the last backup was taken. restorable is false for a backup taken at another database version than the running application.

403.description: Only administrators can see backups.

post.summary: Add a downloaded backup to the server
post.description: Administrators only. Stores a backup file that was downloaded earlier, from this or another installation, so it appears in the list and can be restored. Nothing is restored by this call. The listed date is the moment the backup was taken, not the upload. Send the file as multipart/form-data.

400.description: No file, a file over 100 MB, a file that is not a backup, or one that holds more data once decompressed than the installation accepts (backup.tooLarge).

403.description: Only administrators can upload a backup.

429.description: More than 10 uploads in five minutes; wait and retry.

delete.description: Administrators only. Removes the backup file from the server for good. The data of the installation is not touched.

403.description: Only administrators can delete a backup.

404.description: No backup with this id.

put.summary: Change the note of a backup
put.description: Administrators only. The note is the only part of a stored backup that can change; the file itself is never rewritten.

200.description: The backup with its new note.

403.description: Only administrators can change a backup.

404.description: No backup with this id.

get.description: Administrators only. Streams the stored file, named after the moment the backup was taken. Keep a copy away from the server: a backup that lives only next to the database is lost together with it. The file holds password hashes; treat it as a secret.

403.description: Only administrators can download a backup.

404.description: No backup with this id.

post.summary: Replace all data with a stored backup
post.description: Administrators only. Deletes everything in the installation and loads the stored backup instead, in one database transaction: either the whole file is restored or nothing changes. The caller confirms the action with their current password; a wrong password answers password.incorrect and counts toward the sign-in lockout, and a locked-out account answers credentials.lockedOut. Users, passwords, households, settings and all financial data become those of the backup. The backups kept on the server are files, not data, so the list survives a restore. Every sign-in session is deleted and the caller's cookies are cleared, so the client must send the user to sign in again with a password from the backup; other signed-in users are asked to sign in once their short-lived access token runs out. The backup must come from the same database version as the running application; an older or newer one answers backup.schemaMismatch. A backup that holds more data than the installation accepts answers backup.tooLarge. Rate limited to 5 attempts per five minutes per client.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: The backup id.

200.description: When the restored backup was taken and how many tables and rows were loaded.

400.description: The password is wrong, the file is damaged or too large, or the backup comes from another database version.

403.description: Only administrators can restore a backup.

404.description: No backup with this id.

409.description: The database was busy (lock timeout, deadlock or serialization failure). Nothing was changed; retry.

429.description: Too many restore attempts or too many wrong passwords; wait and retry.

post.description: Sets a spending limit for one category. A category can carry a single budget, so creating a second one for the same category is rejected.

201.description: The budget was created. The Location header points at it.

400.description: Validation failed, the category is not visible to you, or it already has a budget.

get.description: Returns every budget you can see, each with the amount spent against it so far in the current period, so the client can render progress without a second call.

200.description: The budgets visible to the signed-in user.

delete.description: Removes the spending limit. Transactions in the category are untouched.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: The budget id.

404.description: No such budget is visible to the signed-in user.

put.description: Changes the limit, or moves the budget to a different category. Spending already recorded is re-evaluated against the new limit the next time the budget is read.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: The budget id. Takes precedence over the id in the body.

400.description: Validation failed, or the category is not visible to you.

404.description: No such budget is visible to the signed-in user.

post.description: Adds a category for transactions to be attributed to. The flow type is fixed at creation and cannot be changed afterwards, because moving a category between income and expense would silently rewrite the meaning of every transaction already filed under it.

201.description: The category was created. The Location header points at it.

400.description: Validation failed, the name is taken, or the named household is not one of yours.

get.description: Returns your personal categories plus the shared categories of the households you belong to. Each one carries its flow type, so the client can offer income categories and expense categories separately.

200.description: The categories visible to the signed-in user.

delete.description: Removes the category. Transactions filed under it are kept and become uncategorised rather than being deleted along with it.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: The category id.

403.description: Forbidden

404.description: No such category is visible to the signed-in user.

put.description: Renames a category, changes its icon, or moves it between personal and shared. The flow type is deliberately absent: it cannot be changed after creation.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: The category id. Takes precedence over the id in the body.

400.description: Validation failed, the name is taken, or the named household is not one of yours.

404.description: No such category is visible to the signed-in user.

post.description: Records an exchange of one currency for another inside a single account, such as selling euros for dollars at a broker. The sold balance drops, the bought balance rises, and neither side counts as income or expense. An optional fee is booked as an ordinary expense transaction on the same account so it shows in reports and budgets.

201.description: The conversion was recorded. The Location header points at it.

400.description: Validation failed, the account is not visible to you, or no exchange rate exists for the fee.

get.description: Pages through conversions on accounts visible to you, newest first. Rate is the bought amount divided by the sold amount.

parameters.name: accountId
parameters.description: Only conversions on this account.

delete.description: Removes the conversion and the fee transaction it created, restoring both balances.

404.description: No conversion with that id is visible to you.

put.description: Replaces the date, the sold and bought amounts and currencies, the description and the fee of a conversion; the account stays the same. The fee fields describe the fee as it should be afterwards: with feeAmount the linked expense transaction is created or updated (amount, currency, date, category, and its value in the reporting currency at the rate for the new date), without feeAmount an existing fee transaction is deleted. Conversion and fee change together or not at all. A fee transaction that the user has split into lines cannot be changed or removed from here and answers transaction.splitNotAllowed; edit that transaction instead. A conversion imported from a broker (isImported) answers resource.readOnly: correct it at the broker and import again.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: The conversion id. Takes precedence over the id in the body.

400.description: Validation failed, a currency is not enabled, no exchange rate exists for the fee, the fee transaction is split, or the conversion was imported from a broker.

404.description: No conversion with that id is visible to you.

get.description: Returns the currencies accounts and transactions can use, the reporting currency that totals, budgets, and reports are expressed in, and the date of the newest stored exchange rates. Rates are European Central Bank reference rates.
Returns expenses for one month grouped by category, ordered by amount, for the dashboard pie chart. Split transactions contribute to each of their lines separately.

parameters.name: month
parameters.description: Month to report on as YYYY-MM. Defaults to the current month.

200.description: One entry per category that had spending in the month.

get.summary: Get the monthly income and expense trend
get.description: Returns income and expense totals per month, oldest first, ending with the current month. Months with no activity are still present with zero totals so the chart keeps an even x-axis.

parameters.name: months
parameters.description: How many months to include, counting back from the current one. Defaults to 6.

200.description: One entry per month in the requested window.

get.description: Returns the headline figures for the current month: total balance across all visible accounts, income and expenses so far, and the resulting net flow. The month is resolved in the instance time zone, not the caller's.

post.description: Starts tracking money owed. The outstanding amount is subtracted from net worth from the as-of date onwards.

201.description: The debt was created. The Location header points at it.

get.description: Returns the debts you track, each with its outstanding amount, optional interest rate, and the date those figures are as of.

200.description: The debts belonging to the signed-in user.

delete.description: Stops tracking the debt, for instance once it is settled. Snapshots already recorded keep the balance it had.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: The debt id.

404.description: No such debt belongs to the signed-in user.

put.description: Records a new outstanding balance, rate, or name. This is how repayment progress is tracked: lower outstandingAmount as the debt is paid down.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: The debt id. Takes precedence over the id in the body.

404.description: No such debt belongs to the signed-in user.

get.description: Returns how many units of the target currency one unit of the source currency buys, using the newest reference rate on or before the date. Weekends and holidays fall back to the previous business day.

parameters.name: date
parameters.description: Rate date as YYYY-MM-DD. Defaults to today.

200.description: The rate and the date it was published for.

404.description: No rate is stored or reachable for that pair.

post.description: Starts tracking progress towards a target amount, optionally by a target date. The goal is a standalone tracker: it is not tied to an account, and moving money does not update it by itself.

201.description: The goal was created. The Location header points at it.

get.description: Returns your savings goals with the amount saved so far against each target.

200.description: The goals belonging to the signed-in user.

delete.description: Removes the goal and its recorded progress. Nothing else in the ledger changes.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: The goal id.

404.description: No such goal belongs to the signed-in user.

put.description: Changes the name, the target, the target date, or how much has been put aside. This is how progress is recorded: raise currentAmount as money is saved.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: The goal id. Takes precedence over the id in the body.

404.description: No such goal belongs to the signed-in user.

post.description: Creates a household and makes you its owner. A household is the unit that shared accounts, categories, and transactions belong to; adding members is what gives other people sight of that data.

201.description: The household was created. The Location header points at it.

get.description: Returns the households you belong to, each with its member list and their roles. Households you are not a member of are never listed.

200.description: The households the signed-in user belongs to.

delete.description: Disbands the household. Only an owner may do this, and only once nothing shared still points at it: accounts, categories, and transactions shared with the household must be made personal or removed first.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: The household id.

400.description: Shared data still belongs to the household.

403.description: The signed-in user is a member but not an owner.

404.description: No such household, or the signed-in user is not a member.

get.description: Returns a household with its members. A household you are not a member of is reported as missing rather than forbidden, so the endpoint cannot be used to discover that a given household exists.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: The household id.

404.description: No such household, or the signed-in user is not a member.

put.description: Changes the household name. Only an owner may do this; a plain member gets 403 rather than 404, because membership already tells them the household exists.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: The household id. Takes precedence over the id in the body.

403.description: The signed-in user is a member but not an owner.

404.description: No such household, or the signed-in user is not a member.

post.description: Adds an existing user to the household by email address. From that moment they can see every shared account, category, and transaction of the household, so treat this as granting access to financial data rather than sending an invitation.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: The household id. Takes precedence over the id in the body.

200.description: The household with the new member included.

400.description: No such user, or they are already a member.

403.description: The signed-in user is a member but not an owner.

404.description: No such household, or the signed-in user is not a member.

delete.description: Revokes a member and with them their sight of the shared data. The last owner cannot be removed. Data the household owns stays with the household.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: The household id.

parameters.name: userId
parameters.description: The id of the member to remove.

400.description: That user is not a member, or removing them would leave no owner.

403.description: The signed-in user is a member but not an owner.

404.description: No such household, or the signed-in user is not a member.

put.description: Promotes a member to owner or demotes an owner to member. The last owner cannot be demoted, so a household is never left without someone who can manage it.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: The household id.

parameters.name: userId
parameters.description: The id of the member whose role changes.

200.description: The household with the updated roles.

400.description: That user is not a member, or the change would leave no owner.

403.description: The signed-in user is a member but not an owner.

404.description: No such household, or the signed-in user is not a member.

post.description: Writes the rows the user kept from a preview into the ledger. Rows the preview flagged as already present are skipped rather than duplicated, and the response reports how many were imported and how many were skipped.

200.description: Counts of imported and skipped rows.

400.description: Validation failed, or the account is not visible to the signed-in user.

post.description: Parses an exported Swedbank statement and returns the rows it found, each with a suggested category and a flag saying whether a matching transaction already exists in the account. Nothing is written: this call only reads the file, and the client decides which rows to keep before calling confirm. Send the file as multipart/form-data.

200.description: The parsed rows, with suggestions and duplicate flags.

400.description: No file, a file over 5 MB, an unreadable statement, or an account that is not yours.

get.description: One connection per account. The Flex token is write-only and never returned.

200.description: Your connections with the time and outcome of the last sync.

delete.description: Forgets the token and stops automatic sync. Imported entries stay.

404.description: No connection on that account.

put.summary: Connect an account to the Interactive Brokers Flex Web Service
put.description: Stores the Flex Query id and token so the server can download the report once a day and on demand. The token is encrypted at rest. Leave Token empty to keep the stored one.

400.description: Validation failed or the account is not yours.

post.summary: Download and import the Flex Query report now
post.description: Asks Interactive Brokers to run the stored Flex Query, waits for it, and imports it the same way as an uploaded file. Can take up to a minute.

400.description: Interactive Brokers rejected the token or query, or the report could not be imported.

409.description: A security in the report kept colliding with one created at the same time. Nothing was imported; retry.

post.summary: Import an Interactive Brokers Flex Query report
post.description: Reads the Trades, Cash Transactions, Corporate Actions and Open Positions sections of a Flex Query XML report. Stock, ETF and fund trades become buys and sells; currency trades become in-account conversions; dividends, withholding tax, interest and fees become cash entries; forward and reverse splits become split entries with the ratio as new shares per old share; open positions update last prices. Deposits and withdrawals become transfers when a funding account is given and are skipped otherwise. Every entry is matched by its broker id, so importing overlapping periods never duplicates. The import is all or nothing. Other corporate actions (mergers, spin-offs, stock dividends, symbol changes) are not booked: they are counted in skipped and listed per type in skippedCorporateActions. When the report has an Open Positions section, positionMismatches lists every security whose quantity replayed from the entries differs from the quantity the broker reports, which is how an action that was not booked becomes visible; it is null when the report has no Open Positions section.

200.description: Counts of what was imported, already present, and skipped, and the positions that do not reconcile.

400.description: The file is not a Flex Query XML report, an account is unknown, or an exchange rate is missing.

409.description: A security in the report kept colliding with one created at the same time. Nothing was imported; retry.

get.description: Returns open holdings with first-in-first-out cost basis, market value at the last known price, and unrealised gain in each security's own currency. Totals and the per-year income table are in the reporting currency: market value and cost at the newest exchange rate, realised gains, dividends, tax and fees at the rate on each transaction's date. IsComplete is false when a holding has no price or no exchange rate, in which case totals leave it out.

parameters.name: accountId
parameters.description: Only holdings and income on this account.

get.description: Securities are shared by everyone on the installation, because a price is the same for all holders.

parameters.name: search
parameters.description: Matches symbol, name or ISIN.

post.description: Adds a stock, ETF, fund, bond or other instrument that trades can refer to. Open to every signed-in user, because recording a first trade needs it. Symbol and currency together must be unique; the operation only ever adds, it never changes an existing security.

put.summary: Update the details of a security
put.description: Changes symbol, name, ISIN, exchange, type or currency, and optionally the price. Securities are shared by every user of the installation, so only an administrator may change them; anyone who holds the security sets its price through the price operation instead. The currency cannot change once the security has transactions.

403.description: The caller is not an administrator.

404.description: No such security.

409.description: Another security already has this symbol and currency.

put.summary: Set the last known price of a security
put.description: Sets the price by hand. Securities are shared by every user of the installation, so this is open only to a user who currently holds the security on an account they can see, and to administrators. A broker import overwrites the price when its report date is the same or newer.

200.description: The security with its new price.

403.description: The caller holds no open position in this security and is not an administrator.

404.description: No such security.

post.description: Buys and sells need a security, quantity and price, and move quantity times price plus or minus the fee in the security's currency. Dividends, withholding tax, interest and fees need an amount. A split needs a security and a ratio in Quantity and moves no cash. The cash effect lands on the account's balance in that currency and never counts as income or expense in reports or budgets.

400.description: Validation failed, the account or security is unknown, or no exchange rate exists for the date.

get.description: Pages through trades, dividends, withholding tax, interest, fees and splits on accounts visible to you, newest first. CashAmount is signed: negative when cash left the account.

parameters.name: accountId
parameters.description: Only entries on this account.

parameters.name: securityId
parameters.description: Only entries for this security.

parameters.name: type
parameters.description: Only entries of this type.

delete.description: Removes the entry and its cash effect. A later broker import will not bring a deleted imported entry back.

404.description: No such entry on an account visible to you.

put.description: Replaces every field of an entry that was recorded by hand, under the same rules as recording one. Entries imported from a broker are corrected at the broker and imported again. A correction that would leave a later sale without enough shares is refused.

400.description: Validation failed, the entry was imported, the account or security is unknown, or no exchange rate exists for the date.

404.description: The entry does not exist.

get.description: Returns assets, debts, and the difference between them as of now. Account balances count towards assets, so cash in the ledger and tracked assets are not double counted against each other.

200.description: Total assets, total debts, and net worth.

get.description: Returns the snapshots taken by the nightly background job, oldest first. Snapshots are only written while the job runs, so a freshly seeded instance can answer with an empty series.
Returns your notifications, newest first. These are raised by background jobs, for example when a recurring bill is about to fall due.

parameters.name: unread
parameters.description: Set to true for unread only, false for read only. Omit for both.

200.description: The notifications for the signed-in user.

post.description: Clears the unread badge by marking all of your notifications read at once.

patch.description: Marks a single notification as read. Marking an already read notification again changes nothing and still answers 204.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: The notification id.

404.description: No such notification belongs to the signed-in user.

get.description: Answers with a fixed message and the server time in UTC. It touches no database and needs no session, so it checks that the process is up and serving. For a check that includes the database, use /health instead.

post.description: Schedules a bill or a recurring income. Nothing is posted to the ledger on a schedule: the background job raises a reminder before the due date, and a transaction is only written once the occurrence is confirmed.

201.description: The recurring bill was created. The Location header points at it.

400.description: Validation failed, or the account or category is not visible to you.

get.description: Returns your scheduled bills and income, each with its cadence and the date it next falls due. Inactive schedules are included so they can be reactivated.

200.description: The recurring bills belonging to the signed-in user.

delete.description: Removes the schedule and its reminders. Transactions already posted from it stay in the ledger.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: The recurring bill id.

404.description: No such recurring bill belongs to the signed-in user.

get.description: Returns a single schedule with its cadence, reminder lead time, and next due date.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: The recurring bill id.

404.description: No such recurring bill belongs to the signed-in user.

put.description: Changes the schedule, the expected amount, or the reminder lead time. Setting isActive to false stops reminders without losing the schedule or the transactions already posted from it.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: The recurring bill id. Takes precedence over the id in the body.

400.description: Validation failed, or the account or category is not visible to you.

404.description: No such recurring bill belongs to the signed-in user.

post.description: Posts the transaction for one occurrence of the schedule and rolls the next due date forward by the cadence. expectedDueDate identifies which occurrence is being confirmed, so a retry or a double click cannot post the same bill twice.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: The recurring bill id. Takes precedence over the id in the body.

200.description: The posted transaction and the new next due date.

400.description: The due date does not match, the amount is missing, or the account is not visible to you.

404.description: No such recurring bill belongs to the signed-in user.

get.summary: Summarise income and expenses over a range
get.description: Returns income, expense, and net totals for an arbitrary date range, with the per-category split. Unlike the dashboard endpoints, the window is yours to choose rather than being pinned to calendar months.

parameters.name: dateFrom
parameters.description: Inclusive start date as YYYY-MM-DD. Defaults to the start of the current month.

parameters.name: dateTo
parameters.description: Inclusive end date as YYYY-MM-DD. Defaults to today.

200.description: Totals and the per-category split for the range.

get.description: Every signed-in user can read the settings, because they decide which pages, currencies and defaults the client offers. Only administrators can change them.

put.description: Administrators only. Replaces every installation-wide setting. A feature that is turned off answers 404 with code feature.disabled on its routes and its background work stops; its data is kept. Changing the reporting currency revalues every stored transaction at the exchange rate for its own date and fails without saving anything if a rate is missing. Budgets, goals, assets, debts, bills and net worth history keep their numbers.

400.description: Validation failed, or the reporting currency could not be changed because a rate is missing.

403.description: Only administrators can change settings.

post.description: Administrators only. Fetches reference rates published since the newest stored date. It works even when automatic sync is turned off.

200.description: How many rates were added and the newest rate date now stored.

403.description: Only administrators can sync rates.

get.summary: Read the settings the sign-in page needs
get.description: Anonymous. Returns only the installation name and the default language.

post.description: Creates the administrator account on a fresh instance. It works exactly once: once an administrator exists the endpoint answers 409 for good. Rate limited to five attempts per five minutes per client.

200.description: The administrator account was created; its profile is returned.

400.description: The email or password did not pass validation.

409.description: An administrator already exists; setup is closed.

429.description: Too many setup attempts; wait and retry.

get.summary: Check whether first-run setup is needed
get.description: Reports whether the instance still has no administrator. The client calls this before choosing between the setup screen and the login screen. It stays callable without a session and discloses nothing beyond the single flag.

200.description: needsSetup is true while no administrator exists.

post.description: Posts income or an expense to an account. Leave lines empty for an ordinary transaction. To split one payment across several categories, send the lines instead: they must add up to the transaction amount, and the top-level categoryId is then ignored.

201.description: The transaction was created. The Location header points at it.

400.description: Validation failed, the split lines do not add up, or the account or category is not visible to you.

get.description: Returns a page of the ledger, newest first, restricted to what you can see: your own transactions plus those on the shared accounts of your households. Every filter is optional and they combine with AND.

parameters.name: page
parameters.description: One-based page number. Defaults to 1.

parameters.name: pageSize
parameters.description: Rows per page. Defaults to 20.

parameters.name: accountId
parameters.description: Keep only transactions on this account.

parameters.name: categoryId
parameters.description: Keep only transactions in this category, including split lines filed under it.

parameters.name: type
parameters.description: Income or Expense.

parameters.name: search
parameters.description: Case-insensitive match against the description.

parameters.name: dateFrom
parameters.description: Inclusive start date as YYYY-MM-DD.

parameters.name: dateTo
parameters.description: Inclusive end date as YYYY-MM-DD.

200.description: A page of transactions with the total row count.

post.summary: Set the category of several transactions
post.description: Files every listed transaction under one category, or clears their category when categoryId is null. The request is all-or-nothing: if any id is not visible to you, is a split transaction, or has a type the category does not match, nothing changes. Repeated ids count once.

400.description: Validation failed, a listed transaction is split, or the category is not visible to you or does not match a transaction's type.

404.description: At least one listed transaction is not visible to the signed-in user.

get.description: Returns the filtered ledger as a UTF-8 CSV attachment named transactions.csv, with account and category names resolved. It takes the same filters as the list endpoint but ignores paging: every matching row is included. Rows are streamed from the database into the response, so the size of the ledger does not matter.

parameters.name: accountId
parameters.description: Keep only transactions on this account.

parameters.name: categoryId
parameters.description: Keep only transactions in this category.

parameters.name: type
parameters.description: Income or Expense.

parameters.name: search
parameters.description: Case-insensitive match against the description.

parameters.name: dateFrom
parameters.description: Inclusive start date as YYYY-MM-DD.

parameters.name: dateTo
parameters.description: Inclusive end date as YYYY-MM-DD.

200.description: The CSV document as an attachment.

get.description: Renders the filtered ledger as a printable PDF, attached as transactions.pdf. It takes the same filters as the list endpoint but ignores paging. A PDF is built in memory, so it holds at most 5000 rows (App:PdfExportMaxRows); a larger result is refused with export.tooManyRows. Narrow the filters or use the CSV export, which has no limit.

parameters.name: accountId
parameters.description: Keep only transactions on this account.

parameters.name: categoryId
parameters.description: Keep only transactions in this category.

parameters.name: type
parameters.description: Income or Expense.

parameters.name: search
parameters.description: Case-insensitive match against the description.

parameters.name: dateFrom
parameters.description: Inclusive start date as YYYY-MM-DD; also printed in the header.

parameters.name: dateTo
parameters.description: Inclusive end date as YYYY-MM-DD; also printed in the header.

200.description: The PDF document as an attachment.

400.description: More rows match than a PDF may hold.

get.description: Returns the row count and the income and expense totals of every transaction the list endpoint would return for the same filters, across all pages. Transfers are not transactions and are never counted.

parameters.name: accountId
parameters.description: Keep only transactions on this account.

parameters.name: categoryId
parameters.description: Keep only transactions in this category, including split lines filed under it.

parameters.name: type
parameters.description: Income or Expense.

parameters.name: search
parameters.description: Case-insensitive match against the description.

parameters.name: dateFrom
parameters.description: Inclusive start date as YYYY-MM-DD.

parameters.name: dateTo
parameters.description: Inclusive end date as YYYY-MM-DD.

200.description: The count and totals of the matching transactions.

delete.description: Removes the transaction and any split lines, and adjusts the account balance accordingly.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: The transaction id.

404.description: No such transaction is visible to the signed-in user.

get.description: Returns a single transaction, including its split lines when it has any. A transaction you cannot see is reported as missing rather than forbidden.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: The transaction id.

404.description: No such transaction is visible to the signed-in user.

put.description: Replaces the transaction. Split lines are replaced wholesale rather than merged: send the full set you want to keep, or omit lines to turn a split back into a plain transaction. Moving it to another account adjusts both balances.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: The transaction id. Takes precedence over the id in the body.

400.description: Validation failed, the split lines do not add up, or the account or category is not visible to you.

404.description: No such transaction is visible to the signed-in user.

post.description: Moves money from one of your accounts to another. Both balances change and neither side counts as income or expense, so reports and budgets are left alone. The two accounts must differ and both must be visible to you.

201.description: The transfer was created. The Location header points at it.

400.description: Validation failed, the accounts are the same, or one of them is not visible to you.

get.description: Returns a page of transfers between your own accounts, newest first. Transfers are kept apart from transactions on purpose: moving money between your accounts is neither income nor an expense and must not distort reports.

parameters.name: page
parameters.description: One-based page number. Defaults to 1.

parameters.name: pageSize
parameters.description: Rows per page. Defaults to 20.

parameters.name: date
parameters.description: Keep only transfers on this date, as YYYY-MM-DD.

200.description: A page of transfers with the total row count.

delete.description: Reverses the transfer: both account balances go back to what they were before it.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: The transfer id.

204.description: The transfer is gone and both balances are restored.

404.description: No such transfer is visible to the signed-in user.

put.description: Replaces the date, amounts, description and both accounts of a transfer. The amount rules are those of creating one: between two currencies the received amount is required, within one currency it may be left out and must equal the sent amount when given. Send currency and receivedCurrency as the transfer has them; without them they default to the main currency of the chosen accounts. You need access to both accounts the transfer has now and to both accounts it should have afterwards. A transfer that was created or matched by a bank or broker import holds a receipt per imported account, flagged by fromAccountImported and toAccountImported: its date, that account's side of the transfer and the amount on that side are fixed and a change answers value.locked, while the description, the other account and, between currencies, the other amount stay editable.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: The transfer id. Takes precedence over the id in the body.

400.description: Validation failed, an account is not visible to you, a currency is not enabled, or the change touches a value fixed by an import receipt.

403.description: One of the transfer's current accounts is not visible to you.

404.description: No such transfer is visible to the signed-in user.

post.description: Provisions a user account with an initial password. There is no self-service sign-up: accounts exist only because an administrator created them. Administrators only.

201.description: The user was created. The Location header points at it.

400.description: Validation failed, or the email is already taken.

403.description: The signed-in user is not an administrator.

get.description: Returns user accounts with their role and whether they are still active. Filters are optional and combine with AND. Administrators only.

parameters.name: search
parameters.description: Case-insensitive match against the display name or email.

parameters.name: role
parameters.description: Keep only users in this role.

parameters.name: isActive
parameters.description: True for active accounts, false for deactivated ones.

parameters.name: sort
parameters.description: Field to sort by. Defaults to display name.

parameters.name: direction
parameters.description: Asc or Desc. Defaults to Asc.

403.description: The signed-in user is not an administrator.

put.description: Changes your display name and, optionally, your password. A password change needs the current password as well, and refreshes the session cookie so the browser stays signed in. This is the one user endpoint that does not require the Admin role.

400.description: Validation failed, or the current password was wrong.

post.description: Locks the account out instead of deleting it, so the transactions and households it touched stay intact. Existing sessions are rejected on their next request. You cannot deactivate yourself, and the last active administrator cannot be deactivated, so an instance is never left without one. Administrators only.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: The user id.

403.description: The signed-in user is not an administrator or is the target, or the change would leave no active administrator.

404.description: No such user.

post.description: Lifts the deactivation set by the deactivate operation and clears the failed sign-in counter, so the user can sign in again with the password they had. Sessions from before the deactivation stay revoked. Calling it for a user who is already active changes nothing and still answers 204, so it is safe to repeat. Administrators only.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: The user id.

403.description: The signed-in user is not an administrator.

404.description: No such user.

post.summary: Set a new password for another user
post.description: Administrators only. For a user who forgot their password: the administrator chooses a temporary password and hands it over outside the application, and the user changes it on their profile after signing in. The administrator confirms the action with their own current password; a wrong one answers password.incorrect, counts toward the administrator's sign-in lockout, and a locked-out administrator answers credentials.lockedOut. The new password must satisfy the same rules as any other password, otherwise password.tooWeak. Every session of the target user is revoked and their failed sign-in counter and temporary lockout are cleared; a deactivated user stays deactivated. With resetTwoFactor the authenticator is switched off and the recovery codes are invalidated as well, for a user who also lost their device. The target may be a member or another administrator, never the caller: change your own password on the profile. Rate limited to 10 calls per five minutes per client.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: The user id. Takes precedence over the id in the body.

200.description: The profile of the user after the reset.

400.description: The administrator's password is wrong, or the new password is missing or too weak.

403.description: The signed-in user is not an administrator, or is the target.

404.description: No such user.

429.description: Too many attempts or too many wrong passwords; wait and retry.

put.description: Promotes a user to administrator or demotes them to member. You cannot demote yourself, and the last active administrator cannot be demoted, so an instance is never left without one. Role changes and deactivations are applied one at a time, so two administrators demoting each other at the same moment cannot both succeed. Administrators only.
